title: STRAND: Sequence-Conditioned Transport for Single-Cell Perturbations
claim: Conditioning a generative model on the DNA sequence at the perturbation site lets it separate distinct effects of perturbations that share a gene identity.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; input, model stack in center, paired outputs on right
description: The figure reads left to right in three columns. The left panel is titled 'Unperturbed cell'. It zooms from a cell to DNA, then to Gene A between Gene B and Gene C, then to a Gene A-associated genomic region. Two marked sites in that region give two alternative perturbation sequences, s_p^1 (orange) and s_p^2 (magenta), shown as nucleotide strings. Below them, a bar chart shows the unperturbed RNA expression profile. The center column is a blue box labeled STRAND. It stacks a DNA FM, a DNA perturbation module, a cellular transport module and an RNA FM, joined by vertical arrows. The sequence and the expression profile feed in from the left. On the right, two tinted panels, orange and pink, show bar charts of the transcriptomic response for genes A, B, C and N. Dashed lines mark unperturbed levels and arrows mark up or down shifts. The two panels differ for the same gene A, and the word 'or' sits between them.
caption: \textbf{Overview of \method{}.} \method{} conditions perturbation effects on regulatory DNA sequence to perform in-silico profiling of locus-specific perturbations at 128 bp model resolution within a 524 kb sequence context. Perturbations targeting the same gene at different genomic locations ($s_p^1$, $s_p^2$) can induce distinct transcriptional responses.
abstract: Prediction of the transcriptional response of a cell to a genetic perturbation is a central problem in the computational modeling of gene regulation. Perturbations of the same gene can produce different transcriptional responses depending on the targeted locus, such as an alternative transcription start site or a distal regulatory element, and gene-level perturbation models represent these distinct interventions with a single gene identifier. We introduce STRAND, a generative model that encodes the regulatory DNA sequence at the perturbation locus and uses this encoding to parameterize a conditional transport process from control to perturbed single-cell states. Sequence conditioning enables zero-shot prediction for perturbation targets absent from training and supports locus-resolved inputs at 128 bp model resolution within a 524 kb sequence window. On CRISPRi screens in K562, Jurkat, and RPE1 cells, STRAND achieves the best average rank on few-shot and unseen-gene benchmarks, with gains of up to 33% in perturbation discrimination, and improves transfer to held-out cell lines by up to 0.12 in $Î$Pearson. Ablation studies attribute these gains to sequence conditioning and to conditional transport. At the locus level, STRAND distinguishes alternative transcription start sites and validated regulatory elements that gene-identifier models represent as a single perturbation. STRAND is available at https://github.com/mims-harvard/STRAND.
